plan.title: Paired within-subject DE: control vs treated (n=5)
plan.analytical_narrative: Five subjects each contribute a control and a treated blood sample (paired design, no batch). The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — is answered by DESeq2 with a design of ~subject + condition, which removes between-subject variation and tests the within-subject condition effect via the Wald test on the condition coefficient, with apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change. QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) precedes the model to confirm subjects pair correctly and no sample is an outlier. A minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=5 samples, the smaller group size) keeps DESeq2's independent filtering as the primary filter. BH-adjusted p-values at alpha=0.05 select DE genes. Because the DESeq2 Wald statistic is signed and monotone in one coefficient, an unambiguous ranked list exists, but knowledge-service policy for this exact situation (paired n=5, gene-level enrichment) restricts the enrichment method to over-representation analysis (ORA) with an explicit universe of tested genes rather than preranked GSEA — this was verified against the knowledge service (fgsea preranked was flagged as not permitted here) and the plan follows ORA against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways human collections, each with its release stated, and with the required caveat that ORA needs at least ~50 significant genes to have power. A final report step compiles the DE results, fit diagnostics, per-subject concordance of the DE genes, and the enrichment result with full reproducibility metadata (session info, package versions, collection releases).
